channel.title: AI Blog Explainers
channel.description: The AI announcements that matter, from Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google — turned into visual explainers.

item.title: Managing Open-Weight Model Risk
item.description: Microsoft and NVIDIA argue weight-openness isn't a risk rating — an open-weight model's risk comes from its use case, deployment, and safeguards. Their new joint whitepaper gives a shared five-category taxonomy (cybersecurity, data protection, content, human-AI interaction, bias) so teams speak one language, maps each risk to evaluations (Microsoft Foundry adds groundedness, safety scoring, and automated red teaming), and ties every risk to a working control and an accountable owner — revisited as models and deployments change.

item.title: What to Look For in AI Enterprise Search
item.description: Most employees still can't find the file they need, and bolting a chatbot onto a broken index doesn't fix it. Box's guide separates AI enterprise search from keyword search: intent-based, permission-aware retrieval that grounds answers in source documents you can verify. The practical core is a five-capability buying checklist — semantic retrieval, agentic refinement, permission-aware relevance, metadata-driven accuracy, and unified access across silos — plus a four-phase rollout and the metrics to track. Cited stats are third-party.

item.title: Governing Third-Party AI Agents
item.description: AI that advises became AI that acts, so Box argues a clean vendor review tells you nothing about what a single agent can actually do inside your systems. Govern each agent by its access and authority with two separate levers: least privilege (what it can see) and least agency (what it can decide). Enforce boundaries while the agent acts via a five-step cycle, and don't let trust auto-pass down multi-agent delegation chains.

item.title: Getting Unstructured Data AI-Ready
item.description: Agents reason from the messy 80% of enterprise information — documents, scans, contracts, chat. Box's State of AI Report 2026 finds 96% of organizations say agents need company content, yet 49% have already had an AI data-exposure incident and only 34% have formal access rules. The fix is governance plus quality: index and enrich content where it lives, exclude sensitive or stale files before ingestion, and deliver curated datasets instead of file dumps. Box customers have classified more than 7 billion files.

item.title: A First Look at the New Box for Guidewire
item.description: The new Box for Guidewire brings AI document intake and data extraction into insurance claims and underwriting, inside the system of record. Adjusters and underwriters access, preview, and manage Box-hosted documents and metadata without leaving ClaimCenter, PolicyCenter, or BillingCenter, while Box AI and Box Extract auto-classify evidence and pull the data each workflow needs. External parties submit through governed Box intake paths with no Guidewire access, and one insurer is modernizing more than 100 terabytes of content with Box alongside Guidewire.

item.title: Easier Microsoft 365 to Workspace Migration
item.description: Google targets the two things that stall a Workspace move: losing data in transit and users who still live in Office. Data import now moves Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams up to 5x faster at no extra cost (generally available now), and by year-end will preserve Microsoft Information Protection labels and encryption. Office files stay editable in Gmail, Docs, and Sheets (cell capacity doubled to 20 million), and a native Google Meet experience runs on existing Cisco room hardware before year-end.

item.title: Gemini 4 Argon Pushes the Frontier of Enterprise Work
item.description: Box ran Google’s new Gemini 4 Argon through its Complex Work Eval — agents handed real bundles of spreadsheets, PDFs, slides and images and graded on the finished deliverable. It scored 85% overall versus 71% for Gemini 3.1 Pro (+14 points), with the biggest gains in data analysis (+23) and report drafting (+15). Regulated domains moved most: life sciences 61→88, healthcare 57→87 and public sector 76→94. The model is “coming soon” to Box AI; these are Box’s own benchmark numbers, so validate on your own workloads.

item.title: CRM in the Flow of Work, Agents in the Process
item.description: Microsoft is inverting the CRM model — customer context and actions come to people inside Copilot and Teams instead of the other way around. Thirty pre-built Dynamics 365 skills across Sales, Service, and Customer Insights land in Copilot's Cowork, Autopilot, and Code experiences, powered by Dynamics 365 MCP servers. Autonomous agents run whole processes: a Service Agent handles cases end to end across Outlook, Teams, and Office, and a Sales Development Agent builds and qualifies pipeline from its own Exchange inbox (consuming Copilot credits from Nov 16). Dynamics 365 Activate maps a lower-risk path off legacy CRM, and everything is governed through Agent 365.

item.title: GPT-6 and Intelligent UI, for Everyone
item.description: OpenAI is rolling GPT-6 out globally in ChatGPT alongside Intelligent UI, which lets answers come back as interactive charts, buttons, forms and small on-demand tools rather than plain text. GPT-6 Instant starts responding 44% sooner than GPT-5.6 on web-search questions (OpenAI’s own testing); Sol serves Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise while Luna serves Free and Go, and the Work and Codex models are unchanged.

item.title: Claude Haiku 5.5: More Accurate, Half the Latency
item.description: Box ran Claude Haiku 5.5 through its Complex Work Eval — agents that locate documents and reason across spreadsheets, PDFs and slides against weighted rubrics. Haiku 5.5 scored 60% overall versus 49% for Haiku 4.5 (+11 points), used about 27% fewer tokens, and produced deliverables in roughly half the time. The biggest gains were in arithmetic-heavy work — report drafting (+19) and data analysis (+10) — with financial services rising from 48% to 71%.

item.title: 3 Lessons from Frontier AI Vulnerability Research
item.description: Microsoft’s FORGE Lab used AI agents for vulnerability research across Windows and open source, producing 140 Windows CVEs from May to September 2026 and 155 internally validated reports across 23 open-source projects. The takeaway in three lessons: optimize for reproducible findings rather than scan volume, spend reasoning where it removes a specific uncertainty, and fold validation and patching into the discovery loop. As AI finds bugs faster than teams can fix them, the bottleneck shifts from discovery to triage, validation and remediation.

item.title: Automating the Workday with Workspace Studio
item.description: Google's Executive Productivity Advisor shows how she offloads an overloaded workday to Workspace Studio — a no-code command center where plain-English descriptions become background flows that move work across Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Meet, and Chat without a prompt each time. Her own flows run a daily briefing, pull action items into a to-do list, send pre-meeting Chat briefs and post-meeting follow-up drafts, catch spoken commitments from Meet transcripts, and scan department trackers each Friday for blocked work. Flows trigger on a schedule or an event and can carry Gemini 'skills' with team-specific instructions.

item.title: CISO Perspectives: Vulnerability Risk in the Age of AI
item.description: Two Microsoft security leaders make the CISO case that in an AI-accelerated world, remediation — not scanning — is the bottleneck: AI speeds weakness-finding and exploit development alike, and on-premises Patch Tuesday volumes are rising, with September 2026 setting a record near 1,000 vulnerabilities. Their playbook: resource remediation as a planned budget line, shorten patch timing for critical systems to as little as 24 hours, adopt AI scanning and remediation harnesses now, and strengthen defense in depth on the assumption that not every vulnerability will be patched in time.

item.title: Atlassian and OpenAI Expand Their Partnership
item.description: Atlassian is extending its OpenAI partnership so that GPT-6-family models power agents across its platform and Rovo, grounded in the Teamwork Graph — an enterprise context layer linking people, projects, documents and decisions. A product manager can ask whether a launch is on track and Rovo flags blockers, missed milestones and decisions drawn from Jira and Confluence, while Atlassian plugins pull work items and docs into ChatGPT and Codex under existing permissions. More than 3,000 Atlassian developers already use Codex, and the companies are exploring letting teams assign work directly to AI agents.

item.title: Bolt Turns Weeks of Compliance Work into Minutes
item.description: Bolt, the urban-mobility platform operating in 50+ countries with 4,000+ employees and 170,000+ employee documents in Box, faced a compliance backlog that would have taken about two years to audit by hand. It built an HR workflow combining Box Automate (consistent renaming, folder creation and routing), Box Extract (metadata tagging) and Box Apps (a queryable dashboard), pulling documents from both Box and Workday into one content layer. Compliance questions that once took weeks or months — such as how many Belgian employees have a remote-work clause — are now answered in minutes, with staff shifting from manual checks to reviewing AI output.

item.title: How Cresta Built an Agent Builder on the Claude Agent SDK
item.description: Cresta turned years of contact-center expertise into Conductor, a natural-language builder that ships production customer agents on the Claude Agent SDK. It cut first-deployment time by roughly half, and Cresta treats the build as 20% of the job, spending the rest on evaluation and iteration against four task types.

item.title: A Practical Guide to Building with GPT-6
item.description: OpenAI's practical guide to GPT-6 focuses on production discipline: match Astra (hardest reasoning), Sol (near-Astra at a fifth the cost) or Luna (fast everyday) to the workload, cache input tokens for up to 95% savings, specify outcomes rather than rigid instructions, and use mid-turn steering and async tool calling to keep long-running agents productive and supervised.

item.title: Northern Rockies: Governed Public-Sector AI with Box
item.description: Northern Rockies Regional Municipality went from banning AI outright to running it on a governed Box content layer — role-based access, full audit logging, and no training on its data. Box AI now accelerates Freedom-of-Information requests, surfaces technical answers in seconds, governs ingested email via mxHERO, and drafts HR documents with Box Doc Gen, while staff validate outputs and keep the final word.

item.title: Claude Code Mods: Customize the CLI in TypeScript
item.description: Mods are lightweight TypeScript functions that hook into Claude Code’s events to rewrite prompts, block tool calls, add UI, or replace built-ins — shipped inside plugins. On Team and Enterprise plans a built-in sec-default mod loads first so user mods can’t override security rules.

item.title: Barclays Scales Claude Across the Bank
item.description: Barclays is expanding Claude across engineering, customer service, and Global Markets: Claude Code is expected to reach 50% of its developers by end of 2026, a knowledge assistant used by 16,000+ employees has run since 2025, and Claude classifies and routes roughly 120,000 client emails a day — all under robust governance and human oversight.

item.title: Albertsons Reimagines Retail with OpenAI
item.description: Albertsons is expanding OpenAI across 2,200+ stores (Albertsons, Safeway, Vons, Jewel-Osco, Shaw’s, ACME, Tom Thumb) serving 36 million weekly customers — pairing ChatGPT Enterprise for digital, operations, fulfillment, and merchandising teams with customer-facing apps on the OpenAI API, including a Safeway plugin that turns recipes, photos, or meal requests into a built cart with savings and checkout.

item.title: Google Workspace September Drop: Image AI and Interactive Data
item.description: Google Workspace’s September drop brings six AI updates: Google Pics for pro-level object-level image editing and 2K/4K upscaling inside Docs and Slides; Sheets canvas to turn data into one-click interactive mini-apps; Workspace Intelligence for cross-app task automation; a unified Ask Gemini in Chat; Google Vids document-to-video conversion; and Gemini-based data classification in Drive for DLP and retention.

item.title: Claude for Government Is Now Generally Available
item.description: Claude for Government is generally available inside a FedRAMP High authorized environment, with usage-based pricing and hard caps instead of seat fees, tiered admin controls across departmental hierarchies, two-person approvals for sensitive actions, and audit logging. Claude Code and Claude for Microsoft 365 are in early access through the same environment.

item.title: How Anthropic's Sales Team Rebuilt Inbound with Managed Agents
item.description: A Claude-powered buying agent now handles thousands of inbound sales conversations a day across contact, pricing, and in-product surfaces — qualifying leads, answering on the spot, or handing complex deals to reps with full context. Agent-qualified leads convert to opportunities more than twice as often and close about five days faster.

item.title: Box Shield: Classification-Based Access Policy for AI Agents
item.description: Box Shield’s classification-based access policy treats an AI agent reading a file as equivalent to downloading it, and governs Read and Download as separate, independently toggled actions. Every request is evaluated at request time against the file’s current classification and the caller’s integration ID, with restricted reads returning no content at all and every decision logged to the Event Stream API — deployable in monitor mode before enforcement.

item.title: The Playbook for Intelligent Content Workflow Automation
item.description: Box's playbook treats content as one governed lifecycle — plan, create, review, approve, distribute, analyze — rather than manual follow-ups. Choose task-based (predictable but fragile) or status-based (flexible but needs owners) workflows, automate the handoffs with rule-driven Box Relay and agents, and keep editorial, legal, compliance and brand as explicit human checkpoints, with Shield and Governance enforcing access and retention.

item.title: How Asana Builds Human-Agent Teams with Claude
item.description: Asana treats Claude-powered agents as members of the team inside its Work Graph, each with a role, scoped permissions, shared memory and visible output. The result is a shift from prompting agents to coaching them, grounded in three live workflows: Slack support, at-risk renewal briefings, and engineering cycle planning.

item.title: OpenAI DevDay 2026, Unpacked
item.description: OpenAI's DevDay 2026 pushed from chat to delegated, agentic work: always-on Dots agents, GPT-6.1 Sol, an Ultrafast tier up to 8x faster, an Agents API with computer use and managed infrastructure, team collaboration across ChatGPT (Space, Pages, Team Tasks, @ChatGPT in Slack and Teams), Private Intelligence security options, and a 32-partner enterprise marketplace atop 1.2 billion weekly users.

item.title: GPT-6.1 Sol: Near-Flagship Intelligence at a Fifth of the Price
item.description: GPT-6.1 Sol is OpenAI’s new mid-tier model offering near-Astra intelligence for about a fifth of the price. It matches GPT-6 Astra on DeepSWE v1.1 coding at one-fifth the cost, beats Opus 5.5 on document analysis and automation benchmarks for less, cuts factual errors 32% at low reasoning effort, and is available now across ChatGPT tiers and the API as gpt-6-1-sol.

item.title: OpenAI's dots: Always-On Agents That Run With Your Projects
item.description: Dots are frontier agents powered by GPT-6 Astra that work independently 24/7, each with its own sandboxed cloud computer and browser and connections to 4,000+ apps, reachable across ChatGPT, Slack, Teams, and voice. Enterprises can deploy ‘specialist dots’ with dedicated identities, credentials, and access — managed through Microsoft Agent 365 — with sandboxing, auto-review, and custom approval rules built in.

item.title: Making Unstructured Content Programmable with Jev
item.description: Jev is a ‘System One’ model that returns typed values and probabilities instead of open-ended text, so software can consume its judgments directly — no JSON post-processing. Using three primitives (Choice, Score, and Noul), it routes documents to Escalate, Monitor, or Review based on severity, type, and escalation probability, attaching signals as Box metadata while thresholds and review tasks keep humans on consequential decisions.

item.title: Box AI Cuts Security Triage From 30 Minutes to Seconds
item.description: Box’s Security Incident Response Team cut phishing investigation from 30 minutes to seconds by running header, body, and screenshot analyses in parallel, and now auto-closes 56% of phishing cases while escalating sensitive-data references to analysts. Phishing was about 40% of tickets; automation now covers 50–60% of total volume across roughly 20% of alert types, freeing analysts for proactive, hypothesis-driven threat hunting.

item.title: Giving Companies More Control Over Their AI Agents, with NVIDIA
item.description: Anthropic and NVIDIA combined Claude Managed Agents with NVIDIA's open-source OpenShell to give enterprises layered control over autonomous agents. Credentials stay vaulted, every action runs under default-deny policy with full logging, and OpenShell's policy prover mathematically verifies an agent's reach, so companies can limit what an agent does, review what it did, and prove the limits hold.

item.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 on Real Enterprise Knowledge Work
item.description: Box evaluated Claude Sonnet 5.5 on real customer workflows spanning spreadsheets, PDFs, slides and images. Accuracy rose from 61% to 65%, deliverables completed 2.4x faster, and token use fell 12%, with the largest gains in regulated industries, financial services climbed from 63% to 81%. The model fact-checks across documents, catching errors earlier versions propagated.

item.title: Sage Hospitality Automates the Work Behind the Welcome
item.description: Sage Hospitality Group — 60+ hotels and 60+ restaurants — uses Box Forms and Box Doc Gen to automate document work: access requests generate, route and store themselves in the right Box folder at 500+ a week, and vendor contracts live in Box with automatic version control and permissioned sharing. Next up are Box Sign e-signatures, contract dashboards, metadata extraction, and Box Hubs portals.

item.title: Build Plugins for Claude
item.description: Plugins are now the primary way to extend Claude, bundling MCP connectors, Agent Skills, or both. A new directory submission portal lets developers on paid plans submit, track and publish, with automated safety scanning on arrival and post-launch analytics on installs and discovery. The foundation is MCP 2.0, with MCP Apps for in-chat UI and Enterprise Managed Auth for zero-touch OAuth.

item.title: The New Microsoft Copilot: Home, Code and Autopilot
item.description: Microsoft reorganized Copilot around three pillars. Home unifies Chat for interactive work with Cowork for delegated tasks; Code, built on GitHub Copilot, lets non-developers build apps and automations in natural language; and Autopilot runs assigned work autonomously, even while the user is offline. Native Office editing, Fabric IQ and Work IQ grounding, and a new Plugin Registry round it out, with a gradual rollout through the Frontier program.

item.title: Muse Spark 1.3 Comes to Box AI
item.description: Muse Spark 1.3, from Meta Superintelligence Labs, is now available in Box AI for complex enterprise document work. On Box's Complex Work Eval it posts a 13% accuracy edge over similarly priced models, 42% faster completion than version 1.2, and about a third fewer tokens, with financial services accuracy rising from 66% to 75%. It reads image-based tables, normalizes before comparing, and commits to a single interpretation.

item.title: Box and Salesforce: Powering the Headless Enterprise
item.description: Box and Salesforce are building a 'headless enterprise' where governed content and structured business data flow into apps, workflows and AI agents without moving files from their source. Salesforce is the system of record exposed over MCP; Box is the governed filesystem for AI via its MCP server. Agents like Claude, Agentforce and Slack bots reason across both while respecting existing permissions, with Claudeforce adding 37 prebuilt sales skills.

item.title: The 5 AI Agents Every Executive Should Build First
item.description: Google’s executive productivity advisor Laura Mae Martin recommends five AI agents every leader should build first in Gemini Enterprise’s Agent Designer, no code required: a Sentiment Analyst for meeting transcripts, a Schedule Auditor that checks priorities against calendar time, a Daily Briefing agent, an Investor Relations Coach, and a Gratitude Reminder. The advice: start with one recurring task that adds little strategic value, then scale.

item.title: What's New in Microsoft Security: Governing AI Agents
item.description: September’s Microsoft Security updates center on governing AI agents: Defender can now discover AI agents running on employee devices, Entra Global Secure Access extends Zero Trust classification and enforcement to agent traffic, and Purview intercepts on-behalf-of agentic actions to block data from reaching unsanctioned AI tools. The release also covers shadow-AI prevention at the network layer, Purview data-lifecycle controls, and eDiscovery for Copilot Pages and Loop.

item.title: Claude Tag: Personal Connectors in Channels
item.description: Claude Tag can now use the connectors you personally authorized — Drive, calendar, GitHub, a CRM — inside Slack channels, not just DMs. It asks permission on first use, remembers it for the thread, posts in Review or Auto mode, and logs every action under your own account; unattended routines still use channel-level connectors.

item.title: Claude Opus 5.5: Built for Context-Heavy Coding
item.description: Claude Opus 5.5 is tuned for long, context-heavy coding sessions and runs about 40% cheaper than Opus 5 on typical token-billed workloads — standard tokens down 20%, cached reads down 60%, a one-hour cache, subagent forking that reuses the parent's context, and about 30% faster output. Pick the model at session start and keep the cache warm to capture the savings.

item.title: Box for ServiceNow, Natively
item.description: ServiceNow runs the process; Box holds the files — and this native, ServiceNow-certified integration finally puts the content inside the record. A Box panel on each record lets people preview, upload, and share without leaving the ticket, case, or request, and every record gets its own auto-created Box folder across ITSM, HR, CSM, CRM, or custom modules. Files stay in Box with version control, classification, legal hold, and retention intact; it installs in minutes as a certified scoped app with no middleware.

item.title: Scaling on Claude Marketplace with Snowflake and Vercel
item.description: Claude Marketplace, in limited preview, lets a company with an Anthropic commitment direct part of that spend toward partner tools it already uses — such as Snowflake and Vercel — without a new budget request. Power Digital and ThoughtSpot run Claude inside Snowflake (keeping existing governance), while CodeRabbit moved its agents on Vercel from pay-as-you-go to a committed plan funded by its Anthropic commitment, closing the deal in a week. The pattern: pre-approved budget collapses procurement from quarters to days, and sellers reach customers already building on Claude.

item.title: Reimagining the SOC for the Agentic Era
item.description: Microsoft introduced ISOC — an Integrated Security Operations Center in Microsoft Defender that unifies SIEM and threat protection into one system for AI-driven operations. The argument: attackers automate execution at AI speed, so security can’t win with protection and operations as separate stacks. ISOC runs a six-layer autonomous stack and an integrated protection loop, with humans directing strategy and agents handling continuous detection and response.

item.title: How to Prepare for AI-Driven Code Modernization
item.description: Anthropic's playbook for AI-driven code modernization: agents can finish in weeks, but the organizational work doesn't shrink. Define one target (Uplift, Transform, or Reimagine), write a machine-checkable certificate of pass conditions, set a leadership-owned tiered promotion policy, lay the prerequisites, build an agentic workflow you tune rather than each change, then pilot on a small partition before scaling.

item.title: Claude Marketplace: Plugins, Agents & Services in One Place
item.description: The Claude Marketplace is one catalog for 2,000+ connectors and plugins, buyable Claude-powered agents and products (CrowdStrike, Cursor, Harvey, Snowflake), and consulting partners like Accenture, BCG, and Deloitte. Builders list via three paths: MCP/Skills connectors, products sold against committed Anthropic spend, or the Partner Network.

item.title: Microsoft: Building the System for AI at Work
item.description: Microsoft's framing for deploying AI safely, affordably and at scale rests on three pillars: a multi-model platform embedded in Microsoft 365 and grounded in your data; a two-track business model (predictable per-seat USL plus usage-based Copilot Credits with spend visibility and limits); and partnership, with Forward Deployed Engineers handling the change-management and trust side of adoption.

item.title: Anthropic and Accenture on Embedded Evaluation
item.description: Anthropic is partnering with Accenture’s Faculty division to embed independent evaluators with employee-level access — red-teaming models, running alignment assessments, testing safeguards, and monitoring decisions through development and deployment. Both expect to invest at least $1 billion over five years; the arrangement is non-exclusive, with more partnerships, including METR, planned.

item.title: Projects Redesigned: From Folder to Conversation
item.description: Claude Code projects stop being a folder of files and become a coordinator conversation: you describe a goal and a top-level chat splits it into parallel worker threads — each a cloud session on its own branch and repo copy — that run, get reviewed, and are assembled back into the result. A shared project memory and a library keep decisions and artifacts consistent across threads, and you tune check-in cadence plus the model and effort for the coordinator and workers. In beta for select Pro and Max cloud-session users, with Team and Enterprise to follow.

item.title: How Balyasny Evaluates & Governs Claude Fable 5
item.description: Balyasny Asset Management (~$38B AUM) grades every model on thousands of its own financial tasks: Claude Fable 5 hit 89.4% accuracy versus 86.1% for the prior model and cut merger-arb deal analysis from three-to-five days to under one. Its BAMAgent platform runs thousands of agents 24/7 under least-privilege access, logging, and human review, so a more capable model never gets wider authority by default.

item.title: Claude Cowork and Chat Are Now One Claude
item.description: Claude Cowork and chat are merging into one Claude: you no longer pick a mode before starting — Claude figures out what a task needs — and Cowork and Design capabilities work from any conversation. New Claude Docs and Slides let you co-write documents and have Claude draft editable decks you can present or download as PowerPoint or PDF, while existing chats, projects, artifacts, connectors and skills carry over. Claude can keep working after you close your laptop, you can check progress from your phone, and you set how often it checks in. It’s rolling out to Pro and Max users over the coming weeks, with Team and Free to follow.

item.title: Skills in Google Workspace: Teach Gemini Your Team's Know-How
item.description: Skills in Google Workspace are reusable AI prompts — built with your organization’s rules, templates, and reference files — that guide Gemini to automate repetitive tasks and turn individual expertise into institutional knowledge. Teams author them in Google Docs, deploy via Workspace Studio, and invoke them with @ mentions across Gmail, Docs, Slides, and Drive, with a skills marketplace and admin curation on the way.

item.title: Microsoft 365 G7: Copilot and Governed Agents for Government
item.description: Microsoft 365 G7 is a government-grade productivity and AI suite for U.S. GCC environments, combining Copilot across Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Teams (grounded by Work IQ), mission-focused agents for policy, casework, grants, and constituent services, and an Agent 365 control plane to discover, register, and govern every agent. It builds on M365 G5 and the Entra Suite, with phased GA from October 1.

item.title: OpenAI's Agents API: Orchestration as a Service
item.description: OpenAI opened the orchestration engine behind Codex as the Agents API (public beta): define task, model, tools, and environment in one call, and it manages context compaction, hosted or self-hosted sandboxes, and parallel subagents. You pay only for tokens and tool use; early customers report up to 60% lower cost, 4× lower latency, and 86% fewer failed responses.

item.title: ChatGPT for Financial Services, Data Included
item.description: ChatGPT for Financial Services pairs GPT-6 Astra with built-in datasets (Daloopa, PitchBook, LSEG News, Crunchbase) and entitlement passthrough for sources firms already license, plus admin-published Office templates and SSO/SCIM/RBAC governance. GPT-6 Astra scores 69.9% on OfficeQA Pro versus 60.2% for GPT-5.6 Sol; design partners include Morgan Stanley and Evercore.

item.title: A Data Agent That Skips the SQL
item.description: ChatGPT Work's new Data agent lets non-technical users query warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift) in plain language, investigate changes, and build interactive dashboards — no SQL. It runs inside governed BI tools (Tableau, Power BI, Sigma, ThoughtSpot) and grounds answers in company semantic layers and dbt metric definitions.

item.title: T. Rowe Price Puts Claude at the Core of Investing
item.description: T. Rowe Price expanded Claude across its investment organization — professionals use Cowork for research synthesis and multi-step operations, and developers build tools with Claude Code. AI leadership sits inside Investments and Global Distribution, T. Rowe Price Labs evaluates and scales applications, and each business unit owns its apps under responsible-use standards.

item.title: Describe an App, Copilot Builds It
item.description: Microsoft's Copilot Cowork and Copilot Studio turn a plain-language description into a working full-stack business app via agentic coding — connected to org data through connectors and Work IQ, able to take actions and write back to Microsoft 365. Apps respect Entra identity and policy by default, and IT manages published apps from the Microsoft 365 admin center.

item.title: Box Content, Now Inside ChatGPT
item.description: Box and OpenAI embed Box content directly in ChatGPT: browse the folder hierarchy, @mention files as context, preview sources beside the chat, and edit Box Notes — without duplicating content. Existing Box permissions decide what's reachable and admins control which MCP server tools users can invoke; generally available now, rolling out to ChatGPT paid tiers.

item.title: Turn a Spreadsheet Into a Mini App
item.description: Google's Sheets canvas, powered by Gemini 3.8 Flash, turns spreadsheet rows into interactive mini apps from a plain-language prompt — Kanban boards, executive dashboards, financial scenario models, schedules, 2×2 matrices, and workshop boards. Visual edits sync back to the underlying data, and everything lives in the sheet and shares with normal file permissions.

item.title: Five Cross-App Agents Inside Google Workspace
item.description: Google Workspace added five agentic capabilities that finish cross-app tasks without switching apps: Chat to Slides, Drive to Sheets, Docs to Gmail, Gmail to Docs, and Docs to Slides. Each keeps you in the app you're in while Gemini carries the content across; available on Business/Enterprise Standard and Plus, AI Pro/Ultra, and Education plans.

item.title: Metadata: The Layer That Makes Enterprise AI Work
item.description: Box's guide for CDOs and IT leaders argues enterprise AI stalls on unreachable content, not models: 96% of organizations want agents to reach company content but only 36% of adopters have connected them. The fix is a governed five-stage extraction pipeline (ingest, classify, extract, validate, act) whose fields inherit source permissions and lineage — Barnett Capital cut underwriting 60× and Makena Capital search from ~1 hour to ~1 minute.

item.title: Cutting Claude Costs 50–73% Without Losing Quality
item.description: Anthropic's platform team shows three levers cut Claude API costs 50–73% while holding or improving accuracy: byte-exact prompt caching, pruning instructions written for older models (14.6% cheaper and 5.3% more accurate on an Opus 4.8→5 migration), and calibrating effort per task. The automated cost-optimizer cut LegalBench 58%, tau2-bench retail 73%, and SWE-bench 55% with median steps dropping 29→17.

item.title: Box Mount: A Filesystem for Sandboxed Agents
item.description: Box Mount maps Box folders into sandboxed AI-agent environments as ordinary POSIX directories, so agents use standard filesystem APIs while Box handles two-way sync and stays the governed system of record — permissions, versions, retention, Shield, and audit intact. It's framework-agnostic (OpenAI, Anthropic, LangGraph, CrewAI, Python) and built for contract review, RFP drafting, and multi-agent document work; available in private preview.

item.title: 6 Ways Workspace Intelligence Personalizes Help
item.description: Workspace Intelligence gives Gemini a real-time, unified understanding of your work across Gmail, Drive, Chat, Docs, Slides and Sheets, so help is personalized with no prompts or setup — daily briefings, one-shot drafts in your voice, on-brand decks, and live spreadsheets from natural language. It respects existing file permissions, isn't used for ads or training without permission, and stays under admin control.

item.title: Box Tests GPT-6 Astra on Enterprise Work
item.description: On Box's multi-document business benchmark, GPT-6 Astra scored 77% overall versus GPT-5.6 Sol's 74%, pulling far ahead on the hardest legal, energy, and technology tasks by labeling proxies, citing clauses, and flagging data-quality issues.

item.title: Box Agent in Apps: Deep Agents In-Platform
item.description: Box embedded an autonomous reasoning agent inside Box Apps that breaks a goal into subtasks, reads across dozens of documents, and returns a traceable, source-linked answer — all under existing Box permissions with no data movement.

item.title: The Anatomy of Effective Commerce Agents
